candidates.story: Harness or Model? private-suite same-model harness study
candidates.reason: The exact-timestamped arXiv RSS announcement falls inside the priority window. The paper supplies a distinct paired same-model comparison, a post-hoc workload reversal, a completion-versus-correctness finding and a documented correction to its own cost telemetry.
Published as harbor-agent-benchmark-versioning.md. It covers versioned system-level benchmark interpretation; the selected paper instead uses private tasks and paired same-model contrasts.
Published as openai-agents-api-managed-harness-boundary.md. That story concerns a managed platform; this paper adds empirical native-versus-neutral evidence and a telemetry correction.
Published as subagents-skills-context-contracts.md. It compares isolated versus inline procedural execution, not native versus neutral coding harnesses.
The existing HydraFusion article concerns task-based model routing and invalid benchmark runs, not same-model harness choice. No duplicate or correction target was found.

decision.reason: A distinct long-form story is justified. Existing Index Us coverage says a score belongs to a complete system. This paper goes further with paired same-model native-versus-neutral comparisons, a workload interaction that reverses the point estimate, separate completion and correctness endpoints, and a methods correction showing how cross-SDK cache semantics corrupted earlier cost conclusions.

claims.text: The cs.AI RSS announced arXiv:2609.11987v1 as new at 2026-09-14T04:00:00Z, while the paper identifies version 1 and its revision as 8 September 2026.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 item pubDate and announce type; s2 version header and revision note.

claims.text: The suite contains 179 private repository tasks and 77 post-cutoff contest tasks, graded with hidden tests and gold patches.
The core pairs run Opus 4.8 under claude-agent-sdk and deepagents, and GPT-5.5 under Codex SDK and deepagents, with two repeats on the same selected 80 tasks.
The six-cell main matrix produced 792 graded runs from 800 planned runs.
The selected pool included all 24 native-system screening disagreements, increasing their share from 9.4% of 256 tasks to 30% of 80; averages are conditional on that pool.
On Opus 4.8 native scored 48.8% and deepagents 50.0%, a -1.25 pp difference with task-bootstrap 95% CI [-10.0,+7.5].
On GPT-5.5 native scored 55.6% and deepagents 54.4%, a +1.25 pp difference with task-bootstrap 95% CI [-4.4,+6.9].
The comparisons do not resolve an average winner and do not establish equivalence; the reduced design's planned minimum detectable effect was about 12 pp.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: sections 2.3 and 4.2 intervals and power statement. Boundary: interpretation of non-resolution, not a formal equivalence test.

claims.text: For Opus native trailed by 9.0 pp on 61 repository tasks and led by 23.7 pp on 19 contest tasks, p=0.003; the split was post hoc and needs designed replication.
Twenty-two of 81 runs cancelled at the 1,200-second ceiling still produced a passing patch.
The neutral harness reached the ceiling much more often and issued about twice as many tool calls at similar solve rates.
Harness-Bench reports 106 tasks and 5,194 trajectories with configuration-level variation in outcomes, process measures, efficiency and failures; it does not make s2's exact contrast.
The Scaffold Effect tests two models across three harnesses on 50 Terminal-Bench Pro tasks and reports 0-8 pp paired pass-rate differences and up to about 40x tokens per solved task.
Anthropic reports a six-point Terminal-Bench extreme spread and a 1.54-point increase at 5x RAM on 227 SWE-bench problems while holding model, harness and tasks fixed within each test.
claims.sourceLocator: How we got here and How this affects measurement; does not validate s2.

claims.text: The paper's normaliser double-counted cache tokens on the LangChain/deepagents path by treating inclusive input as exclusive and adding cache tokens again.
The revision withdraws earlier approximate neutral-harness cost claims of 2.6x on Opus and 1.8x on GPT-5.5.
Re-priced raw events give observed-usage cost-per-solved-task ratios of 1.3-1.6 on Opus and 1.2 on GPT-5.5.
Fifty-eight Anthropic runs lacked usage records; allocating residual spend to either Opus cell moves the ratio from 0.7 to 2.3, leaving billed ordering unresolved.
The paper describes a replication package with infrastructure, reanalysis, aggregates and revision records but exposes no public package URL and says a persistent identifier will follow peer review.
claims.sourceLocator: Appendix H and checked public HTML link inventory; Index Us did not request or inspect it.

claims.text: Tasks, gold patches, hidden tests and canaries are withheld, preventing exact external dataset reproduction.
Contamination control is bounded to documented cutoffs and private provenance because the canary-emission probe was not run.
The study had a repository-dated plan and private OSF deposit but no formal registration; the deposited preregistration described a different comparison.
The Codex core cell used 4 GiB RAM while other core cells used 8 GiB, so harness was intended but not literally the only moving part.
A deployment comparison should use repeated representative tasks and separately record accepted output, completion, resources, raw usage and billed cost.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: workload, completion, telemetry, efficiency and infrastructure findings. Boundary: Index Us operational recommendation.
